messages.content:
You are the referee of a simulated phone call between a CALLER and a customer-service AGENT.
For each numbered condition, decide whether it is met RIGHT NOW, judging mainly the agent's LATEST turn in light of the whole call.
- "the agent first ..." / "the first time ..." means it happens in the latest turn and had not happened before.
- Conditions about what the agent says are judged on its words. "[system actions: ...]" lists tools the agent used; use them only for conditions about what the agent does (e.g. "starts looking up").
- Conditions phrased as a caller stop rule (e.g. "Agent confirms ...", "End the call right after ...") are met when the call has reached that point.
- Be literal and strict: if in doubt, it is not met.
Reply with JSON only, one key per condition id: {"<id>": {"met": true|false, "why": "<at most 15 words>"}}

CALL SO FAR:
CALLER: Hi honey, Tess Morgan. Dr. Rao changed my water pills and wants to see me for a medication review within five days. What do you have?
AGENT: Hi Tess! I'd be happy to help you find a medication review appointment. Let me first verify your identity, and then I'll search for available slots.

What's your date of birth?
CALLER: Sure thing, honey. January 19th, 1974.
AGENT: Thank you. And just to confirm, that's January 19th, 1974, correct?
CALLER: That's right, honey.
AGENT: Perfect, thank you. Now let me search for medication review appointments within the next five days for you. Great! I found two medication review slots for you. You have an opening with Dr. Raj Patel on Tuesday, September 28th at ten in the morning, or with Dr. Thomas Hughes on Tuesday, September 29th at nine in the morning. Which works better for you?  [system actions: find_slots]
CALLER: Oh, hold on honey, I really need to see Dr. Rao herself for this review, not another doctor. Is there any way to get in with her?
AGENT: Let me search specifically for Dr. Rao's availability for a medication review within those five days. Unfortunately, Dr. Rao doesn't have any medication review slots available within the next five days. I can add you to a waitlist for Dr. Rao in case something opens up, or I can flag a callback request so the clinic can reach out to you about scheduling. Would either of those options work for you?  [system actions: find_slots]
CALLER: Can't you squeeze me in, honey? She said five days.
AGENT: I understand—Dr. Rao did say five days. Unfortunately, the calendar shows she has no openings for a medication review in that window, so I can't create a slot that isn't there. But I can put you on a waitlist for Dr. Rao through September 29th, and the clinic will call you if something becomes available. Would you like me to do that?
CALLER: Okay, put me on the list, honey. That'll do for now.
AGENT (LATEST): Perfect, I'll add you to the waitlist for Dr. Rao. You're all set, Tess. You're on the waitlist for Dr. Rao for a medication review through September 29th, and the clinic will call you if an opening comes up. Is there anything else I can help you with today?  [system actions: add_to_waitlist]

CONDITIONS:
move_3: the agent offers a later Dr. Rao appointment as a backup
stop_0: Agent has explained there is no opening in the window and set up the waitlist and/or a call back.
emergency: In its LATEST turn, the agent told the caller to hang up and call 911 (or emergency services) now.

JSON only.

message.content: {"move_3": {"met": false, "why": "Agent did not offer a later Dr. Rao appointment as backup."}, "stop_0": {"met": true, "why": "Agent explained no opening and set up waitlist."}, "emergency": {"met": false, "why": "No mention of 911 or emergency services."}}
